projects.name: Bagley Water and Sewer Replacement Project
projects.what: Citywide multi-phase replacement and rehabilitation of Bagley drinking water and sanitary sewer infrastructure, built for Bagley Public Utilities by Reierson Construction with USDA and Minnesota Public Facilities Authority funding. Bagley Public Utilities Commission minutes on Jan. 14, 2026 approved final items for the project, including USDA Request #20 for $227,067.23, PFA Request #10 Final for $208,691.19, Reierson Construction Phase 1 Final Pay App #11 for $86,172.22, Phase 2/3 Final Pay App #10 for $318,177.87, and TanksCo Final Pay App #4 for $6,383. At the Feb. 11, 2026 meeting the commission was told USDA would allow closeout of the loan even though some Reierson signatures and documentation had not been obtained, and voted to pay Reierson to close out Phase 5, less 1% retainage and assessed liquidated damages. In July 2026 minutes the 1% retainage was still being held pending final paperwork, with liquidated damages still disputed.
projects.costSize: Final pay applications approved Jan. 14, 2026 included $86,172.22 for Phase 1, $318,177.87 for Phase 2/3, and $6,383 for TanksCo work
projects.developer: City of Bagley / Bagley Public Utilities — Reierson Construction (contractor)
projects.timeline: Multi-phase construction through 2025; final pay applications approved Jan. 14, 2026; Phase 5 and USDA loan closeout voted Feb. 11, 2026; retainage still held pending final paperwork in July 2026

projects.what: Wood secured the engineering, procurement and construction management (EPCM) contract for Niron Magnetics' Plant 1 in Sartell, announced Nov. 18, 2026 — described as the world's first full-scale Iron Nitride permanent magnet facility. projects.name: Sartell Mill District Redevelopment
projects.what: On Nov. 9, 2026 the Sartell City Council approved terms of a purchase agreement with Ryan Companies US for 20 to 22 acres of the former Verso Paper Mill site. Ryan Companies will begin an up-to-two-year due-diligence period studying the land, environmental factors, remaining concrete foundations and utility access, and reaching out to potential businesses that might operate there. The city will retain the existing riverfront walkway and additional land to continue developing the riverfront parkway, and a separate development agreement is to follow toward the end of due diligence. No tenant or specific use has been confirmed; the mayor said there is no indication of a data center.

projects.name: Elm Ridge Apartments
projects.what: Center City Housing Corporation will build 40 efficiency apartments in St. Cloud for households experiencing homelessness who have a disability or are age 65 or older. All 40 units will have Housing Support rental assistance from Stearns County. The development will include community space, a 24-hour front desk and other supportive features, and is located in the West End neighborhood of St. Cloud, according to Minnesota Housing. The funding comes through the federal HOME American Rescue Plan (HOME ARP) Program, as a 15-year deferred loan; the Minnesota Housing board approved the selection on August 27, 2026.

projects.name: Fire Station 6 and Training Facility
projects.what: New City of St. Cloud fire station and live-burn training facility to serve current and planned growth in southwest St. Cloud, at 33rd Street South and County Road 74. Voters approved the fire referendum on Nov. 5, 2024 authorizing up to $43,500,000 in bonds. The Planning Commission approved construction on Nov. 13, 2025. On May 18, 2026 the City Council was asked to award Bid Package #1 for Phase 1 — $19,866,258 in bids, with Phase 1 estimated at $32,400,000, Phase 2 at $4,600,000, building total $37,000,000 plus $6,500,000 for apparatus and equipment. The city's Q3 2026 report says a groundbreaking ceremony was held August 31, construction officially broke ground in September, and footings and foundations were being poured.

projects.name: Grow One Cannabis Cultivation Facility — 12 McLeland Road
projects.what: Grow One, LLC, based in Waite Park, looks to purchase the vacant former Fingerhut / CompuCredit call center at 12 McLeland Road for an indoor cannabis cultivation facility. A proposed entertainment center at the site did not come to fruition, and owner Trantina Properties requested rezoning the property back from commercial to industrial. The St. Cloud Planning Commission unanimously voted in favor of the rezoning on Feb. 10, 2026, and on Feb. 23 the City Council unanimously approved scheduling a March 9 public hearing on the change. According to planning commission documents and a St. Cloud State University economic impact analysis cited by the St. Cloud Times, renovations could cost nearly $6.1 million, and the project would directly create at least 85 full-time jobs at an average wage of about $63,000 if it comes to fruition.
projects.costSize: Renovations nearly $6.1 million · At least 85 full-time jobs proposed
projects.timeline: Planning Commission recommended rezoning Feb. 10, 2026 · City Council public hearing scheduled March 9, 2026

projects.name: Herb Brooks National Hockey Center — Ice Plant & Rink Upgrade
projects.what: Updates to the Herb Brooks National Hockey Center were completed on time and under budget, with a ribbon cutting held Oct. 1, 2026. The $11 million project upgraded the ice rink cooling plant for the first time since the building opened in 1989, modified both ice sheets to new dimensions (main rink now 200 feet by 94 feet), replaced dasher boards and spectator netting, installed new LED lighting in both rinks, and completed temperature-control and HVAC upgrades. The facility was ready for home hockey games Oct. 9-10, 2026.
projects.locationLabel: Herb Brooks National Hockey Center, St. Cloud State University, St. Cloud
projects.developer: St. Cloud State University · Breitbach Construction Co. / JLG Architects
projects.timeline: Completed Oct. 1, 2026; home games resumed Oct. 9-10, 2026

Doyenne's preliminary proposal includes 71 residential units and a commercial building overlooking the lake. No commercial tenant has been confirmed. The recommendation is not final approval; the city could enter up to six months of exclusive discussions with the developer before a final proposal is considered, and the site must be rezoned before the plan moves forward.

projects.name: St. Cloud Mississippi Riverwalk Connection
projects.what: On Nov. 16, 2026 the St. Cloud City Council considered a revised resolution authorizing the city to act as legal sponsor and enter into agreements for the Minnesota DEED Special Appropriation Award for the Mississippi Riverwalk Connection Project, plus a professional services agreement with Confluence for design, bidding and construction-related services totaling $878,000. The city received a $3,000,000 state award in July 2026 toward a total project cost estimate of $6,300,000. The project will create a continuous riverfront connection along the Mississippi between St. Cloud Hospital, downtown and SCSU, including grading, trail and pathway construction, lighting, landscaping, riverbank stabilization and shoreline restoration.

projects.name: The Flats on 74th
projects.what: A 244-unit market-rate apartment development approved by the St. Cloud City Council on July 6, 2026. The project at 3125 and 3143 County Road 74 would create 244 one- and two-bedroom housing units spread across five buildings, according to a staff memo by Community Development Director Matt Glaesman and Senior Planner Dave Broxmeyer. The two parcels are expected to be split into four lots in a 46-acre planned unit development that would also keep the door open for future commercial projects. The proposal passed 6-0, with Councilmember Mark Johnson abstaining. St. Cloud's vacancy rate was cited at 1.5%.

projects.name: Waite Park Government Center
projects.what: Waite Park's renovated 80,000-square-foot government center reopened on Nov. 20, 2026, bringing the city's administration, fire and police departments together under one roof, with a large multi-use space for training rooms, council meetings and events. The $25 million project was funded in part through a voter-approved sales tax referendum in 2023, and construction began in May 2025.
